fields.meta_title: Dropshipping Landing Page Builder With Examples | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a dropshipping landing page from a prompt: a product test, a first-order code, an order lookup, or restock alerts. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Dropshipping Landing Page That Tests Demand First
fields.hero_description: Build a dropshipping landing page that tests a product on real ad traffic and saves every signup to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Dropshipping Page
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the dropshipping landing page and the database that keeps every email the page collects.
fields.feature_1:
A page per product from one prompt

Describe the product and the delivery window your supplier quotes. Emergent builds the page around that offer, with photos up top and a signup form below. Prompt again to change it.
fields.feature_2:
Every signup in a database you own

Each email and restock request the page collects is a row in a database you own. Sort the rows by product, or filter them down to the ad campaign that sent each visitor to the page.
fields.feature_3:
An alert when a count is reached

Pick the number that matters, such as 50 signups on a product test, and the app sends a Slack or email alert when it is reached. Reminders and escalations use the same settings.
fields.feature_4:
Store and supplier data through APIs

The app connects to any tool with an API. An order lookup can read ship dates from the store, and each new signup can sync to the email tool that already sends your campaigns.
fields.feature_5:
Your own domain on each product page

Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. Put each product page on a path or subdomain of the store's domain, and the address in the ad matches the page that loads.
fields.feature_6:
Export the full code to GitHub

On paid plans, Emergent exports the full code to your GitHub repository, from the Standard plan up. The page and its database logic are then yours to host and edit anywhere.

fields.tab_content_1:
Rowanmere orders stock after 87 signups in 5 days

Rowanmere Goods runs ads to a page for a $29 magnetic vent phone mount before ordering stock. Visitors who want one join a notify-me list. In 5 days the ads sent 1,240 visits and 87 people signed up. Makena Odum set 50 signups as her bar, and once the list passed it, the app emailed her to order from the supplier.
fields.tab_content_2:
The PAWS10 code goes out for each email saved

Fennwick Pet Co sells an LED dog collar for $24.00, and its page gives the code PAWS10, 10% off a first order, to any visitor who leaves an email. With the code the collar costs $21.60. In August 310 visitors signed up and 64 of them used the code at checkout, Joaquin Ferrell among them.
fields.tab_content_3:
Order #58316 shows its ship date to the buyer

A buyer on Ossery Trail Co's page types an order number and the email used at checkout. The app reads that order from the store through its API and shows the date the supplier shipped it and the delivery date, with a link to the tracking number. Nova Reyes looked up order #58316: shipped Oct 28, due by Nov 7.
fields.tab_content_4:
Stock returns, and all 142 signups get the email

When Varnum Lamp Co's supplier ran out of its clip-on reading light, the page swapped the buy button for a restock signup. The list reached 142 people. When stock came back on Oct 30, the app emailed all 142 of them, and Ilse Varnum counted 38 orders on the first day.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Dropshipping Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a dropshipping landing page that tests one product and turns its signups into a supplier order.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick one product and one supplier
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the delivery window on the page
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set the count that triggers an order
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose the item for the test, and write down the price you will charge and what each unit costs you delivered. One item per page keeps the ad, the page, and the signup count about the same thing.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask the supplier how long an order takes to reach your buyers, and write that window in plain words near the price. State only a window you can meet, and change the page the day the supplier's times change.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Describe the page in plain English: the product, the price, the delivery window, and what a visitor leaves, such as an email for a notify-me list or for a first-order code. Emergent builds the page and the database behind it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide how many signups justify ordering stock, such as 50, and ask for an email alert when the list reaches it. Write the number down before the ads start, and keep it fixed for the whole test.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Connect the store and the email tool
fields.howto_step_5_des: Link the store to the app, and the order lookup pulls each buyer's ship date from the store's records. Link the email tool that sends your campaigns as well, then pick the list each new signup joins and the tag it carries.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Publish the page at the address the ad will use, under the store's own name. Point one ad set at it first, keep the other ad sets on their old pages, and compare the page's signups with the visits that ad reports.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Order one unit through the store before the ads go wider, then look it up on the order status page. Check that the supplier's ship date shows, the code works at checkout, and the restock email arrives when you mark the item back in stock.

faq_plan.q: What is a dropshipping landing page?
faq_plan.a: A dropshipping landing page is a single page that sells or tests one product a store ships from a supplier. Dropshipping is a retail fulfillment method where a store does not keep the products it sells in stock: the supplier packs the item and ships it straight to the customer. The page carries the offer and the delivery window, with one signup or order step.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a dropshipping landing page?
faq_plan.a: Write a prompt that names the item, what it costs, how long delivery takes, and the one thing a visitor should do. Emergent's AI landing page builder then builds the page with a signup table to match. Publish it on the store's domain, run one ad set to it, and change the page with another prompt as the results come in.

faq_plan.q: What should a dropshipping landing page include?
faq_plan.a: It should include one product with its price and photos, the delivery window the supplier can meet, and one action for the visitor, such as joining a notify-me list or getting a first-order code. Put the return terms near the price, and link to an order lookup page for buyers who already ordered.

faq_plan.q: Can a dropshipping landing page send signups to a CRM?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A page built with Emergent can sync each signup to any CRM or email tool that has an API, along with the product and the ad that brought the visitor in. That is a different job from a crm landing page, which sells CRM software rather than feeding one.

faq_plan.q: How do I test a product with a dropshipping landing page before ordering stock?
faq_plan.a: Run a small ad budget to a page that shows the product and its price with a notify-me signup in place of a buy button. Fix the signup count that would justify an order before the ads start, and order from the supplier only once the list passes it. Tell visitors on the page that it is a launch list, not an order.

faq_plan.q: What shipping times should a dropshipping landing page show?
faq_plan.a: Show the delivery window your supplier can meet, in days, near the price. Under the FTC's Mail Order Rule, a seller must have a reasonable basis for stating or implying that it can ship within a certain time. With no shipment statement, it needs a reasonable basis for believing it can ship within 30 days. Get the supplier's times in writing before the page goes live.

faq_plan.q: When does each product need its own dropshipping landing page?
faq_plan.a: Each product needs its own page when you run ads for it: one ad pointed at one page gives a signup count for that item alone. When visitors browse a niche, such as pet lights or car accessories, a category landing page that lists several products fits better.

faq_plan.q: How do I add a discount code to a dropshipping landing page?
faq_plan.a: Ask for an email, then show the code on the page and send it in a welcome email as well. Create the code in the store's checkout first, with its percentage and any limits, and use the same code on the page. Emergent builds the signup and the email from a prompt, and every address lands in a database the store owns.

faq_plan.q: Can a dropshipping landing page show buyers where their order is?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the store has an API the page can read. The buyer enters the order number with the checkout email, and the page shows the supplier's ship date and a tracking link. Pages Emergent builds can read orders from any store with an API. Show a plain message with the support address when no order matches.

faq_plan.q: Can a dropshipping landing page sell digital products too?
faq_plan.a: It can, but nothing ships, and the supplier steps that shape a dropshipping page drop away: no delivery window, no order lookup, no restock list. Sell the file or the access directly instead. For lessons sold as a program, a course landing page fits the offer better.

plan.angle: Wave 3 page with no top 10 in the workbook and no live SERP (DataForSEO retired); the AlsoAsked tree is about whether dropshipping still pays, not about building the page, so this page wins on what a dropshipping store's page has to do that a general store page does not: test a product before the supplier order, trade an email for a first-order code, answer where-is-my-order from the store's own data, and hold demand while a supplier is out of stock. Four stores, four pages built from a prompt, every signup in a database the owner keeps. The FAQ covers the definition, the build, what the page must show, product tests, shipping-time wording (FTC rule, quoted), discount codes, order lookups, one page per product versus a niche page, CRM sync and digital products. Shopify, ecommerce, Amazon and product pages are siblings and stay out of headings; no checkout or payment processing claims.

intent.evidence: Meta promises a product test, a first-order code, an order lookup and restock alerts; all four are the tabs, plus seven build steps and a comparison.

specificity.evidence: Dropshipping vocabulary: 'the delivery window your supplier quotes', 'notify-me list', 'what each unit costs you delivered', 'one ad set'.

craft.evidence: QC Q2/Q5/Q7 clean; FAQ 3's 34-word sentence reads as one list.

voice.evidence: Concrete details: '$29 magnetic vent phone mount', 'order #58316: shipped Oct 28, due by Nov 7', 'Ilse Varnum counted 38 orders on the first day'.

truth.evidence: feature_5 'Put each product page on a path or subdomain of the store's domain' implies Emergent can serve a page at a path of a store hosted elsewhere, beyond the ledger entry custom-domain ('Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits'). Everything else checks: dropshipping definition and FTC Mail Order Rule lines match their quoted spans (30 days kept, 'ship' not 'deliver'); numbers agree ($24.00 less 10% = $21.60, 87/1,240 = 7%, 142 sent, 38 orders); table is the unedited library set Unbounce, Landingi, Wix.

distinct.evidence: Stories are dropshipping-only (supplier ship date lookup, notify-me test before stock); shopify, ecommerce and amazon primaries stay out of headings.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, answer-first, hub link in item 2, sibling links (crm, course landing page), no brands or formats in questions; paa --spec 0/0.
